## SK Hynix Commits to $38 Billion HBM Buildout Amid Valuation Discount Debate

A $38B commitment cements HBM as a multi-year capex supercycle rather than a one-cycle trade. For AI memory exposure — SK Hynix directly, and NVDA/AMD as HBM consumers — this is structural demand confirmation. The valuation discount angle is separately worth tracking: if the market re-rates HBM demand durability, SK Hynix is the most direct derivative.

- SK Hynix is backing a $38 billion HBM capacity buildout.
- Coverage questions whether the stock's valuation discount is too steep given this capex commitment.
- The buildout is framed as a direct response to AI-driven HBM demand.
- Story is high-confidence; intersects HBM competitive landscape and AI infrastructure capex themes.
